overall: The AG found the Hadley Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving the January 20 and February 3, 2026 minutes late, found the February 17 minutes timely, and declined to audit 2019–2025 minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board routinely failed to approve meeting minutes in a timely manner from 2019 through February 2026.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review whether all minutes of Board meetings held during the seven-year period between January 2019 and February 2026 have been timely approved as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Alleged untimely approval of minutes from the January 20 and February 3, 2026 meetings, which were approved April 21, 2026.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board failed to timely approve these two sets of minutes, as the minutes were not approved within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following each meeting.

allegations.summary: Reviewed whether minutes of the February 17, 2026 meeting were approved timely; they were approved April 7, 2026, the third meeting after.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board approved these minutes in a timely manner.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements for timely approval of minutes.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
